A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASIDE research work. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The clipped Ignore-attack example in v4 remains recoverable from its embedded text.

before.justification: v3 reports original instruction-tuning experiments, separation and utility measurements, prompt-injection evaluations, and representation and intervention analyses in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds Qwen3-8B evaluations and a rotation-angle ablation in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The proposed method still applies a fixed 90-degree isoclinic rotation to data-token embeddings, using supplied token roles, followed by supervised instruction-tuning. The new implementation code clarifies this procedure; alternative angles are tested as ablations.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain Alpaca, SEP, AlpacaEval, BIPIA, Structured Query, TensorTrust, Gandalf, Purple and RuLES, including their existing task scenarios. Qwen3 adds a model configuration. LLMail-Inject and the new deployment examples provide context rather than additional evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate Vanilla and ISE against ASIDE, with pretrained Base models included in separation, utility and representation comparisons. SFT and Vanilla PT labels are standardized to Vanilla. Qwen3 uses the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: v4 adds Qwen3-8B under the existing training and evaluation framework and an experiment training Qwen3 variants with eight rotation angles from pi/8 to pi. Previously reported splits, training budgets, metrics, decoding settings and probing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 and the new Figure 7 test how instruction-data separation depends on rotation angle. Existing linear probing, concept activation, successful-versus-unsuccessful injection analyses, embedding interventions and downstream representation comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: The new angle-ablation figure adds error bars labelled mean plus or minus variance, without specifying its repetition count or variance calculation. Existing three-run standard deviations in Table 1 and standard errors in Table 3 remain unchanged; no increase in their run counts is reported.

E6.justification: All retained numerical rows in Tables 1, 3 and 4 are identical. v4 adds Qwen3 results, angle-sweep results and cross-model summaries. For example, Qwen3 SEP is 71.4% for ASIDE versus 45.3% for Vanilla, while ISE has lower TensorTrust attack success than ASIDE, 19.8% versus 22.4%. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: Definition A.1 and Equation 1 retain the same isoclinic-rotation mathematics. v4 replaces the stacked-embedding notation with an equivalent per-embedding description and explains coordinate swapping and negation at 90 degrees. No substantive theorem, proof or formal-property change is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: parameter-free architectural role separation improves instruction-data separation and prompt-injection robustness under benign instruction-tuning while preserving utility. Additional model evidence and revised emphasis do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 makes deployer-controlled role assignment and resistance to delimiter-based role hijacking explicit, interprets the angle ablation as establishing 90-degree optimality, and emphasizes the strength of Vanilla. The conclusion omits v3's explicit open questions about reasoning tasks and model-generated instructions, while retaining the single-turn limitation.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents chunkwise tokenization, segment_ids, masked rotation code and deployment examples; Appendix A explains the coordinate-swap shortcut. Section 9 reports README instructions and an independent repository rebuild check. The repository address, training hyperparameters, hardware and training-time information were already supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to FIDES, LLMail-Inject, Qwen3, LLMs as software components, and SQL-injection and buffer-overflow defenses. These extend the deployment context and complementary-defense discussion while retaining the existing architectural positioning and relationship to ISE.

P1.justification: v4 revises the introduction, baseline description, safety-results narrative and conclusion, and moves existing benchmark descriptions from Section 5 to Appendix D. It adds implementation, LLM-usage and reproducibility sections and removes acknowledgments, while preserving the overall method–experiments–analysis organization.

P2.justification: v4 adds the angle-ablation figure and expands Figure 2 and Tables 1, 3 and 4 for Qwen3. The safety overview is redrawn, replacing its Llama 2 7B panel with Mistral results already tabulated in v3. Conference formatting reflows existing displays and clips the Ignore-attack box on page 24.

improvement.justification: Implementation guidance and the added model and angle experiments offer benefits, but new reporting errors obscure the net quality gain. Section 5.1 describes an ISE improvement on StruQ-OOD, whereas Table 1 averages show worse attack success: 50.8% versus Vanilla's 45.0%. New Qwen3 in-domain averages in Table 4 conflict with their displayed component scores. Figure 7 also contradicts the claimed monotonic decline above 90 degrees. These inconsistencies prevent a reliable judgment that the additional evidence improves the paper overall.
